source_caption: Isle of Dogs has a few different meanings. On the surface, it’s a story about the bond between people and their pets, showing loyalty, friendship, and not giving up on those you love. But it also says something bigger about the world — including power and control, environmental problems, and how society often treats outsiders. With its unique style and storytelling, the film gently encourages viewers to think about how we treat those who are different or pushed aside.

source_details.title: Isle of Dogs
source_details.synopsis: Isle of Dogs (Japanese: 犬ヶ島, Hepburn: Inu ga Shima) is a 2018 stop-motion animated science fiction comedy-drama film written, produced, and directed by Wes Anderson, narrated by Courtney B. Vance and starring an ensemble cast consisting of Bryan Cranston, Koyu Rankin, Edward Norton, Liev Schreiber, Bill Murray, Bob Balaban, Jeff Goldblum, Scarlett Johansson, Kunichi Nomura, Tilda Swinton, Ken Watanabe, Akira Ito, Greta Gerwig, Akira Takayama, Frances McDormand, F. Murray Abraham, Yojiro Noda, Fisher Stevens, Mari Natsuki, Nijiro Murakami, Yoko Ono, Harvey Keitel and Frank Wood.
